name: hyp-54-half
comment: HALF THE {5,4} PENTAGON — the hyperbolic twin of the dodecahedron board, and the second non-triangular half-tile. Four pentagons meet at every {5,4} vertex, so each corner is 90 degrees; a pentagon has no halving diagonal, so the cut is the MIRROR from a vertex to the midpoint of the opposite edge and the halves are 45-90-90-90 QUADRILATERALS. Scalene and chiral. Sides: the {5,4} edge 1.061275062, half of it 0.530637531, and the mirror segment 1.469351744 — the long edge exactly twice the short one once again. D=8 because 45 degrees is one unit of 2pi/8; the angles are [1,2,2,2] and sum to 7 against the 8 a FLAT quadrilateral would, so the deficit is 1 unit = 45 degrees = pi/4, the tile's area. The sides are DECLARED, not derived: a hyperbolic n-gon has 2n-3 degrees of freedom against n angles, so a triangle is pinned by its angles and a quadrilateral is not. They come from the standard regular-polygon relations, cosh(circumradius) = cot(pi/5)cot(pi/4) and cosh(side) = cosh^2 R - sinh^2 R cos(2pi/5), and the development is what checks them.
